info.name: Filmpire API
info.description:
Complete API collection for testing all Filmpire microservices through the API Gateway, with request tracing.

Infrastructure Flow:
1. Request → API Gateway (localhost:8080)
2. Gateway → Eureka Service Discovery (localhost:8761)
3. Eureka → target service (movie-service:8081, user-service:8082, actor-service:8083)
4. Service → TMDB API (external) / PostgreSQL / MongoDB / Redis as needed
5. Response with caching where applicable

Two API surfaces are tested:
- **Native /api/v1/** (folders 1–12): ApiResponse-wrapped, camelCase, HATEOAS endpoints.
- **TMDB v3 Facade** (folder 13, #33): bare TMDB-path endpoints (/movie/*, /person/*, /genre/*, /discover/*, /search/*) the React app calls — TMDB field names, snake_case, same response shapes the app expects from api.themoviedb.org.
- **TMDB Auth & Account Proxy** (folder 14, #33): `/authentication/*` and `/account/*` proxied to the REAL api.themoviedb.org — login and per-user lists are the one part Filmpire does not clone. Runs green without a login; see that folder's description for the browser-approval step needed to exercise the authenticated path.

HATEOAS: single-resource GET endpoints (movie/actor details, user profile) advertise navigation via `_links`. Movie details return the HATEOAS resource bare (top-level `_links`); actor details and the user profile stay inside the shared ApiResponse envelope, so their links live under `data._links` instead.

Auth: run '8. User Service - Auth → Register' first (or 'Login' if you already have an account) to populate the access_token/refresh_token collection variables used by every '9. User Service - Profile & Lists' request.

item.name: 12. Schema-Drift Self-Healing (#46)
item.description:
Verifies ADR-011: a MongoDB document written by an OLDER version of the Movie model must be treated as a cache miss (evicted + re-fetched from TMDB), not surfaced as a 500.

Before ADR-011 this was a permanent failure: the read threw, so save-through never ran, so the bad document was never rewritten — every subsequent request failed identically until someone deleted it by hand.

SETUP (run once, outside Postman — Postman cannot write a shape the app refuses to write):

  podman exec filmpire-mongo mongosh -u admin -p "${MONGO_ROOT_PASSWORD}" \
    --authenticationDatabase admin filmpire --quiet --eval '
      db.movies.deleteOne({tmdbId: 550});
      db.movies.insertOne({tmdbId: 550, title: "Fight Club",
        overview: "STALE - pre-ADR-010 document",
        spokenLanguages: ["English", "German"]});'

`spokenLanguages` as an array of strings is the pre-ADR-010 shape; the current model expects embedded SpokenLanguage objects.

Then run this folder. The first request heals the document; the second proves the heal persisted and is served locally.

item.name: 14. TMDB Auth & Account Proxy (#33)
item.description:
The gateway's transparent proxy to the REAL api.themoviedb.org for the two things Filmpire cannot clone: authentication and per-user account data (`/authentication/**`, `/account/**` -> `PrefixPath=/3`).

Unlike folder 13, these requests leave the local stack and hit TMDB. The browser never holds the TMDB key: the gateway strips any client `api_key` and injects the server-side one, forwards `session_id` untouched, and relays TMDB's status AND body verbatim.

RUNS GREEN WITHOUT A LOGIN. Each request asserts the authenticated payload when {{tmdb_session_id}} is set, and TMDB's verbatim error body when it is not — so CI (which gates on this whole collection) stays green while still covering the contract.

To exercise the authenticated path (issue #33 AC2/AC3), either:

A. UNATTENDED — set {{tmdb_username}} and {{tmdb_password}} (or TMDB_USERNAME / TMDB_PASSWORD, which smoke-test.sh forwards) and run the folder once. 'Proxy: Approve Token with TMDB Login' approves the token from credentials, no browser involved. Never commit those values.

B. BROWSER — run 'Proxy: Create Request Token', open the approval URL it logs, approve it while signed in to themoviedb.org, then re-run the folder.

Either way the session is created, {{tmdb_account_id}} is resolved from it, and the favorites/watchlist requests execute against the real account.

Requires the gateway to be started with a valid TMDB_API_KEY.

request.description:
Step 1 of the real TMDB login flow (issue #33 AC2). The browser sends NO api_key — the gateway injects the server-side one, so a 200 here proves the proxy route, the key injection and the upstream call all work.

Stores the token in {{tmdb_request_token}} and logs the approval URL. TMDB has no unattended approval path, so a human must open that URL before "Proxy: Create Session" can succeed.

exec: pm.test('TMDB issued a request token (server-side api_key was injected)', function () {
// Hand the token to the session step below. Useless until a human approves it.
console.log('Approve this token in a browser, then re-run this folder:');

item.name: Proxy: Client api_key is stripped and replaced

request.description:
The React app may send its own api_key. The gateway must strip it (RemoveRequestParameter) and inject the server key (AddRequestParameter) before forwarding.

TMDB's two rejection codes make the outcome unambiguous, which is what makes this load-bearing rather than decorative:
  status_code 3 ("Authentication failed")  -> a VALID key was used, only the session was missing. The strip+inject worked.
  status_code 7 ("Invalid API key")        -> the fake client key reached TMDB. The filter is broken.

Deliberately probes /account rather than /authentication/token/new: requesting a token has a side effect. TMDB returns the SAME request_token for repeated calls and resets its approval state, so a second token request silently invalidates the approval the login flow below depends on — which is exactly the bug this request used to cause.

exec: pm.test('Client api_key was stripped, not forwarded (status_code 3, never 7)', function () {
pm.expect(body.status_code, 'status_code 7 means the fake client key reached TMDB')

item.name: Proxy: Approve Token with TMDB Login (optional)

request.description:
OPTIONAL, and the only way to close AC2/AC3 without a browser.

TMDB approves a request token either by a human clicking Approve on themoviedb.org, or through this endpoint, which approves it directly from account credentials. Filling {{tmdb_username}} and {{tmdb_password}} therefore turns the whole login flow — approval, session, account, favorites, watchlist — into an unattended run.

DO NOT COMMIT CREDENTIALS. Both variables ship empty. Supply them per-run instead:
  newman ... --env-var tmdb_username=you --env-var tmdb_password=secret
or via TMDB_USERNAME / TMDB_PASSWORD, which smoke-test.sh forwards for you. Setting them as collection variables in the Postman UI writes them into this file — use a Postman *environment* instead.

Left empty (the CI default) TMDB answers 400/status_code 26, which is asserted as an error-passthrough case so the request is never a no-op.

exec: // pm.variables resolves the whole scope chain. Credentials normally arrive as an
// ENVIRONMENT var (newman --env-var, or smoke-test.sh forwarding TMDB_USERNAME), so
// reading collectionVariables here would always see the empty default and mis-branch.
pm.test('Credentials approved the request token', function () {
console.log('Token approved without a browser — Create Session will now succeed.');
// No credentials supplied: TMDB rejects the empty login. Assert the relay.
pm.test('Missing credentials are relayed verbatim (status_code 26)', function () {
console.log('tmdb_username/tmdb_password not set — skipping the authenticated path.');
// Credentials were supplied but TMDB refused them.
pm.test('Bad credentials are relayed verbatim (status_code 30)', function () {
console.warn('TMDB rejected the supplied credentials — check tmdb_username/tmdb_password.');

item.name: Proxy: Create Session (needs an approved token)

request.description:
Step 2 of the login flow. Exchanges an APPROVED request token for a session_id.

With no approval this returns 401/status_code 17 ("Session denied") — itself worth asserting, since it proves the gateway relays TMDB error bodies verbatim rather than substituting its own. Once the token is approved, by either route (the browser URL logged by request 1, or the credentials request above), this returns 200 and stores {{tmdb_session_id}}, which unlocks every account request below.

exec: pm.test('Approved request token is exchanged for a session_id', function () {
console.log('session_id stored — the account requests below now run authenticated.');
// No human approved the token, so assert the error-passthrough contract instead.
console.log('Token not approved — asserted TMDB error passthrough instead.');
